title: First Things First
author: Stephen R. Covey
A. Roger Merrill
Rebecca R. Merrill
target_audience: Fans of Stephen Covey’s prior work, especially 'The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People'
Anyone struggling with prioritizing demands and managing time
core_themes: Moving from urgency addiction to importance-driven action
Aligning daily actions with personal mission and values
primary_purpose: To teach readers how to organize their lives around what is most important, rather than what is most urgent, by using a principle-guided approach to time management and life effectiveness.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational, instructive, and reflective, with a blend of conceptual frameworks and practical advice
structure_format.organization: Divided into thematic sections; includes models, frameworks (such as the Time Management Matrix/quadrants), and reflective exercises
features: Diagrams and charts (including the Urgency/Importance matrix)

key_concepts_lessons: Traditional time management tools (lists, calendars, prioritization) tend to focus on efficiency and urgency, rather than real importance.
The Urgency/Importance matrix (Quadrant II living) helps identify activities that are important but not urgent—key to long-term effectiveness.
Clarifying personal values, mission, and vision provides an anchor for daily decision-making.
Living reactively to ‘urgent’ demands leads to stress and reduced life satisfaction.
A proactive, principle-centered approach aligns actions with what matters most and brings deeper fulfillment.
notable_features: Expansion of Covey’s time management philosophy introduced in 'The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People'
Introduction and exploration of the Time Management Matrix
Emphasis on defining a personal mission statement
cultural_historical_context: Coming in the wake of 'The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People,' 'First Things First' addressed the 1990s business and personal development world's deep focus on time management and productivity, shifting the conversation from efficiency to effectiveness and authentic living. The book offered an antidote to the era’s 'busyness' and growing work-life imbalance concerns.
reception_impact: Praised for reframing time management from ‘urgent’ to ‘important’ tasks
Widely adopted in business, educational, and personal development communities
Influenced productivity literature and modern goal-setting tools
Some readers found its conceptual nature and exercises more demanding than popular quick-fix productivity books
comparable_titles: The 7 Habits of Highly Effective People by Stephen R. Covey
Essentialism: The Disciplined Pursuit of Less by Greg McKeown
Eat That Frog! by Brian Tracy
Getting Things Done by David Allen
